A circular (Circos-style) plot wraps a genome — or any ordered set of segments — into a ring, stacks
several **data tracks** around it, and draws **ribbons** for relationships between positions. In
Python the usual tool is `pyCirclize`. Here we build an interactive one with
[canvasxpress](https://pypi.org/project/canvasxpress/), from a single portable spec.

## Install

```bash
pip install canvasxpress
```

## The data shape

The matrix is **tracks × segments** (rows are the tracks you draw, columns are the positions around
the ring). A sample annotation segments the ring (here into chromosomes), and `circularConnections`
is a list of `[colour, from, to]` ribbons.

```{python}
import random
random.seed(8)

segments = [f"s{i+1}" for i in range(80)]
tracks   = ["Expression", "Methylation", "CopyNumber", "Density"]
data_m   = [[round(random.gauss(0, 1), 2) for _ in segments] for _ in tracks]

region = [f"chr{i//20 + 1}" for i in range(80)]
cols   = ["rgb(220,40,40)", "rgb(40,120,220)", "rgb(40,160,60)", "rgb(240,150,20)"]
conns  = [[random.choice(cols), random.choice(segments), random.choice(segments)] for _ in range(18)]
```

## The plot

`circularTrackGraphType` picks a renderer per track (`bar`, `heatmap`, `line`, `dot`),
`circularTrackGraphWeight` sets each track's radial thickness, and `segregateSamplesBy` splits the
ring by the annotation.

```{python}
from canvasxpress.canvas import CanvasXpress
from canvasxpress.render.jupyter import CXNoteBook
from IPython.display import display

data = {"y": {"vars": tracks, "smps": segments, "data": data_m}, "x": {"Region": region}}
config = {
    "graphType": "Circular",
    "circularConnections": conns,
    "circularTrackGraphType": ["bar", "heatmap", "line", "dot"],
    "circularTrackGraphWeight": [30, 20, 25, 25],
    "circularTrackName": [1, 2, 3, 4],
    "segregateSamplesBy": ["Region"],
    "title": "Circos-style multi-track plot with connections",
}

cx = CanvasXpress(render_to="circ", data=data, config=config, width=560, height=560)
for part in CXNoteBook(cx).render():
    display(part)
```

Each ring is one track; the inner ribbons are the connections. Hover a segment to read its values;
swap the matrix and ribbons for your own genomic tracks and interactions.

## Why "reproducible"

The matrix, the connections and the `config` **are** the figure — one portable JSON spec that renders
the identical circular plot from R or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
